topics.title: 1. Computer Basics, Generations, Devices & Software
topics.theory:
- **Generations:** 1st = vacuum tubes (ENIAC = Electronic Numerical Integrator And Computer, first all-electronic; **EDVAC = Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer**), **2nd = transistors**, 3rd = ICs, 4th = microprocessors (VLSI), 5th = AI/ULSI.
- **Parts of CPU:** ALU (arithmetic & logic), **Control Unit (the "nervous system" — directs and coordinates)**, registers; the CPU is the "brain" of the computer. Computer properties: speed, accuracy, diligence ("no I.Q." — works for hours without tiring), storage, versatility.
- **Input devices:** keyboard, mouse, **joystick**, scanner, **OMR (optical mark reader — reads answers to tests/surveys)**, **OCR** (text), barcode reader, MICR (cheques). **Output:** monitor, printer, plotter, speaker. **Impact printers:** **dot-matrix**, daisy-wheel, line printer; **non-impact:** inkjet, laser, thermal.
- **System software** (OS, compilers, assemblers, linkers, loaders, device drivers, utilities) vs **application software** (Tally = accounting, MS Office, browsers, DBMS applications). Batch file extension **.BAT**.
- **Information attributes:** accuracy, timeliness, relevance, completeness (isolation is not one). **Unicode** is the universal character set (UTF-8/16/32); **ASCII** is 7-bit (128 chars) / 8-bit extended, handles one language (English) or at most a few; characters have an assigned **collating sequence**. **Floating point numbers** = numbers with decimal point.
- **Memory units:** bit < byte < KB < MB < GB < TB < PB < EB < ZB < YB (each ×1024). **Supercomputer speed = FLOPS** (floating-point operations per second). **Embedded computers** use microcontrollers.
- **Privacy on social media:** avoid sharing personal info, check privacy settings.

qs.stem: Which generation of computer used transistor?
qs.sol:
The use of transistors marks the second generation of computers (roughly 1959–1965).

First generation computers used vacuum tubes; they were large and generated a lot of heat.

Second generation computers replaced vacuum tubes with transistors, making them smaller, faster, more reliable, and more energy-efficient.

Third generation computers used integrated circuits (ICs), and fourth generation computers use microprocessors.

Therefore, transistors were used in the second generation of computers.

qs.sol: Impact printers create images by physically striking an inked ribbon against paper. Physical contact alone does not define impact printing: rollers and heated print heads can touch paper without a striking mechanism.

topics.title: 2. CPU Organisation, Registers, Instruction Formats & Addressing Modes
topics.theory:
- **CPU registers:** **PC/IP (Program Counter) holds the address of the next instruction**; **IR** holds the current instruction; **MAR** (address of memory location being accessed), **MDR/MBR** (data exchanged with memory); **AC (accumulator)**; **SP (stack pointer — holds address of stack top)**. I/O buffer register holds data being exchanged. **Instruction cycle** (fetch → decode → execute) = the processing for a single instruction.
- **Instruction format fields:** **opcode (operation to perform)**, **address field(s)**, **mode field** (addressing mode). Opcode with n bits → **2ⁿ operations**. **Mnemonics** = abbreviations for opcodes.
- **CPU organisations by address count:** **single-accumulator (one-address)** — implied AC (LOAD A: AC ← M[A]); **general register** (two-/three-address: ADD R1, A, B = three-address); **stack** (zero-address, PUSH/POP, postfix). Zero-address uses stack.
- **Addressing modes:** **Implied**, **Immediate (operand in the instruction)**, **Register** (operand in register), **Register indirect**, **Direct**, **Indirect** (2 memory references to fetch operand — 1 for address, 1 for operand), **Relative**, **Indexed (index register + address part)**, **Base register**, displacement mode EA = A + (R). **1 mode bit distinguishes direct vs indirect.** Register, immediate, implied modes do not need memory reference for operand.
- **RISC vs CISC:** RISC = few simple instructions, fixed-length, hardwired control, many registers, load/store, pipelining; CISC = many complex variable-length instructions, **microprogrammed control**.
- **Control unit:** hardwired vs **microprogrammed** (control memory with microinstructions; next-address generator = **microprogram sequencer**; some organisations need no decoder). Flynn: **MISD = Multiple Instruction stream, Single Data stream**, SISD, SIMD, MIMD. **Branch (BR ADR)** loads ADR into PC.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a RISC processor?

An instruction set specifies the operations a processor can perform and how operands are represented. Simpler, regular operations reduce the work needed to decode and execute each instruction.

Pipelining overlaps stages of successive instructions. Instruction latency and the rate of completing instructions are different measures, so a design goal must be distinguished from a universal timing guarantee.

Application

RISC means Reduced Instruction Set Computer. Its classical design uses simple operations, regular instruction formats and relatively few addressing modes to keep the control logic simple. …

Concept

Random access means a memory location can be selected by its address without reading all preceding locations. Volatility describes whether stored data survives removal of power.

In the conventional computer memory hierarchy, the processor uses main memory for active programs and data, while cache holds nearby copies to reduce access time.

Application

A running program places its instructions and working data in main RAM. A load or store instruction identifies an address in that memory.

The CPU issues the memory request through the memory system. A cache hit may supply a load; on a miss, the requested data is fetched from main RAM through the memory controller. …

(ii) Zero-address instructions are applicable to a special memory organization called a stack.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true about control unit?
 I. It manages and coordinate the entire computer system.
 II. It does not perform any actual processing  on data.

Step 2: The control unit does not perform actual data processing such as arithmetic or logical operations. These tasks are handled by the ALU. Therefore, statement II is also correct.

Step 3: Since both statements I and II are accurate descriptions of the control unit's functions, the correct choice is the one that includes both.

qs.stem: What happens when branch instruction “BR ADR” is executed?

topics.title: 3. Assembly Language & the 8085 Microprocessor
topics.theory:
- **Assembly vs machine language:** machine language = binary, machine dependent, hard to modify; assembly uses **mnemonics**, translated by an **assembler** (**pseudo-instructions/directives are for the assembler**, e.g. ORG, END, EQU); **macro** invoked by its name (not CALL/JMP). **Comment symbol in 8085 assembly: `;`**. User-defined tokens = labels/names (e.g. ABC; A, SP, PSW are reserved registers). **END directive** tells the assembler the program ends.
- **8085 (8-bit):** **MVI A, 32H** = move immediate (2-byte instruction, loads 32H into A); **MOV A, B** = register copy (1 byte); **LDA addr** = load accumulator from memory address (3 bytes); **ADD B** adds B to A (1 byte, result in A); **ADI data** = add immediate 8-bit data to accumulator (2 bytes); **JMP addr** = jump to new program location; STA, LXI, PUSH, POP, CALL, RET. Registers A, B, C, D, E, H, L, SP, PC, flags (S, Z, AC, P, CY). 16-bit address bus → 64 KB.
- **Accumulator-based evaluation of Y = (A−B)/(C+D×E):** LOAD D, MUL E, ADD C, STORE T, LOAD A, SUB B, DIV T, STORE Y.

topics.title: 4. Memory — RAM, ROM, Cache, Disk & Storage
topics.theory:
- **Memory hierarchy (fast→slow, small→large):** registers → cache → main memory (RAM) → secondary (disk, tape) → tertiary. **Only main memory (primary) and cache communicate directly with the CPU.** Auxiliary/tertiary memory do not.
- **RAM** = Random Access Memory (volatile, read/write; any location same time). **SRAM** cell = **flip-flops**, faster, costlier, used for cache; **DRAM** = capacitors (needs refresh), cheaper, main memory. **Three forms typically volatile & semiconductor:** SRAM, DRAM (RAM family). ROM/PROM/EPROM/EEPROM/Flash = non-volatile. **DIMM (Dual Inline Memory Module)** = PCB with DRAM chips mounted on both sides. **Random-access** = access time constant regardless of location; sequential (tape), direct (disk).
- **Cache mapping:** **direct**, **associative**, **set-associative**; direct mapping maps each main-memory block into **exactly one** possible cache line. **Write policies:** **write-through** (update both) vs **write-back** (only cache updated during write; main memory updated on replacement).
- **Addressing arithmetic:** n address lines → **2ⁿ** locations (10 lines → 1024; 16 lines → 64K; 2K×16 memory → **11 address lines, 16 data lines**; 64K×8 → 16 address, 8 data lines). Chips needed = total capacity ÷ chip capacity (128K×8 bits ÷ 16K×1 = **64 chips**). A 16 KB memory decodes using higher address lines (A0–A13 select within chip, A14–A15 decode).
- **Magnetic disk:** surfaces → **tracks → sectors → cylinders**; **seek time** (head to track) + **rotational latency** (wait for the sector under head) + transfer time. **Magnetic tape:** sequential access, large capacity, cheap, not direct access. Hard disk can serve as virtual-memory extension. **Unit of transfer:** main memory = number of bits read/written at a time (word), external = block.

qs.stem:
Identify the valid cache organization techniques: 
(i) Direct
(ii) Associative 
(iii) Set-associative
qs.sol:
Cache mapping technique is the rule that decides which cache line (or lines) a given block of main memory is allowed to occupy. Computer architecture recognizes exactly three such techniques: direct mapping (each block maps to exactly one specific line, found from the block address), (fully) associative mapping (a block may be placed in any line, so every line's tag must be compared to locate it), and set-associative mapping (the cache is divided into sets; a block maps to one specific set but can occupy any line within that set, combining the previous two ideas).

The stem lists exactly these three schemes as (i) Direct, (ii) Associative, and (iii) Set-associative. …

qs.stem: A cell of the SRAM is made with ______.
qs.sol: SRAM (Static Random Access Memory) cells are constructed using flip-flop circuits, specifically a latch configuration made of cross-coupled inverters. This design allows the cell to maintain its stored data state as long as power is supplied, without needing periodic refreshing. A standard SRAM bit cell typically uses six transistors to form this stable latch, ensuring fast access times and high reliability. In contrast, DRAM (Dynamic Random Access Memory) cells store data using capacitors that leak charge over time and require refreshing. Magnetic dipoles or magnetic cores are associated with older technologies like magnetic core memory or modern MRAM, not standard SRAM. …

qs.stem: What is a key difference between system software and application software?

opts.A: System software includes programs like web browsers, while application software includes operating systems.
opts.B: System software is designed for end-users, while application software is designed for system administrators only.
opts.C: System software operates the computer hardware, whereas application software is designed to perform specific user-oriented tasks.
opts.D: System software is optional for computer operation, while application software is mandatory.

qs.sol:
System software supplies the operating environment: it allocates memory, controls devices and provides services that programs use. Operating systems and device drivers belong to this category.

Application software uses those services to carry out user tasks such as browsing, editing documents or processing accounts. Comparing the two roles identifies hardware operation versus specific user-oriented tasks as the distinction.

qs.stem: When n bits are used to represent an operation (op) code, then how many different operations a computer can perform?

This is because each bit doubles the number of possible codes. For example, with 1 bit, there are 2 codes (0 and 1); with 2 bits, there are 4 codes (00, 01, 10, 11), and so on. qs.stem: How many bits are required to distinguish between a direct and an indirect address?
qs.sol: To distinguish between two mutually exclusive addressing modes, only one binary digit is necessary. This single bit can encode the two distinct states required for direct and indirect addressing within standard instruction sets.

qs.stem: With respect to size, which of the following represents the correct relationships between different categories of cache memory?
qs.sol: In computer architecture, cache memory sizes increase as we move down the hierarchy. Level 1 (L1) cache is the smallest and fastest, while Level 2 (L2) and Level 3 (L3) caches are progressively larger but slower. Therefore, the correct size relationship is L1 < L2 < L3.

Concept

Width expansion: 1 byte = 8 bits, so each bank needs 8 one-bit chips in parallel.

topics.title: 5. I/O Organisation, Buses & DMA
topics.theory:
- **Data transfer modes:** **Programmed I/O** — CPU constantly monitors (polls) the peripheral status register and stays in a loop (busy-waiting; CPU initiated); **Interrupt-driven I/O** — device signals when ready; **DMA** — data transferred **directly between I/O device and main memory without CPU** (CPU only initiates). DMA types: **burst (block) mode** — a block of words transferred in one sequence (preferred for fast devices like **magnetic disks**), **cycle stealing**, transparent.
- **DMA handshake:** DMA controller requests the bus with **Bus Request (BR)**; CPU grants with **Bus Grant (BG = 1)**, then CPU tri-states its buses and the DMA controller drives address/read/write lines. **Interface** (I/O module) resolves speed/format differences between the CPU and peripheral. **Data input command** = reads a data item from the peripheral into the interface buffer.
- **System bus:** **data bus** (carries data; **width = number of lines**), **address bus**, **control bus** (controls access to and use of the data and address lines; read/write, interrupt, clock). **Bus arbitration** decides who controls the bus (time to coordinate = arbitration time). **Interrupt priority:** daisy chaining decides which source is serviced first (priority interrupt system).
- **Standards:** **SCSI = Small Computer System Interface** (itself a bus); **PCI = Peripheral Component Interconnect**, **PCIe = PCI Express**; USB; serial vs parallel (serial = bit by bit, longer distances; parallel = multiple bits at a time, short distance, faster over small range).

DMA controller / डी.एम.ए. कंट्रोलर: This allows data to be transferred directly between memory and a peripheral device without CPU intervention. …

qs.sol: The width of a data bus is the number of lines or bits it can carry in parallel at one time. For example, a 32-bit data bus has 32 lines and can transfer 32 bits simultaneously. Therefore, the correct term is width.

qs.stem: With respect to Peripheral Component Interconnect (PCI), the letter 'e' in PCIe stands for:

opts.B: Read line act as input line and write line act as output line from DMA

topics.title: 6. Computer Arithmetic, Floating Point & Micro-operations
topics.theory:
- **Sign bit:** **0 = positive, 1 = negative** (signed magnitude/2's complement MSB).
- **IEEE 754 floating point:** **single precision = 32 bits: 1 sign + 8 exponent (bias 127) + 23 mantissa/fraction**; **double precision = 64 bits: 1 + 11 exponent (bias 1023) + 52 mantissa**. Value = (−1)^s × 1.f × 2^(e−bias). 0 10000011 100101… → exponent 131−127 = 4 → 1.1001010 × 2⁴ = 11001.01₂ = 25.25.
- **Normalisation:** mantissa adjusted so the most significant digit is non-zero (1.xxx or 0.1xxx); (0.10101)₂ = 0.10101 × 2⁰ in normalised form. **Alignment** of exponents happens before add/subtract.
- **Booth's algorithm** multiplies signed binary numbers efficiently using recoding of the multiplier (pairs Qn, Qn+1: 10 → subtract multiplicand, 01 → add).
- **Micro-operations** (register transfer): **four types — register transfer, arithmetic, logic, shift**. `R3 ← R1 + R̅2 + 1` = R1 plus the 2's complement of R2 (**subtraction R1 − R2**). Logic micro-ops on 4-bit R1 = 1010, R2 = 1100: AND = 1000, OR = 1110, XOR = 0110.
- A control unit specifies the micro-operations to be executed (via control words in microprogram).

qs.stem: How will (0.10101)2 be represented using normalised scientific notation?
qs.sol: To normalize the binary number (0.10101)₂, we must express it in the form 1.xxxx × 2ⁿ. Currently, the binary point is before the first non-zero digit. Shifting it one position to the right gives 1.0101. To maintain equality, we multiply by 2⁻¹. Thus, the normalized form is 1.0101 × 2⁻¹.

qs.stem:
What is the meaning of this arithmetic micro-operation?
 R3 ← R1 + R̅2 + 1

opts.A: Content of R1 plus R2 transferred to R3
opts.B: Content of R1 plus the 2’s complement of R2 transferred to R3
opts.C: Content of R1 plus the 1’s complement of R2 transferred to R3
opts.D: Content of R1 plus R2 after increments transferred to R3

qs.sol:
The given micro-operation is: R3 ← R1 + R̅2 + 1.

Step 1: R̅2 represents the 1’s complement of R2. This means each bit of R2 is inverted (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0).

Step 2: Adding 1 to the 1’s complement of R2 gives the 2’s complement of R2. This is a standard method to represent negative numbers in binary arithmetic.

Step 3: Therefore, R3 gets the sum of R1 and the 2’s complement of R2. This operation effectively performs R1 - R2 in binary arithmetic. …

qs.stem:
The 4-bit registers R1 and R2 initially have the following values.
 R1 : 1010
 R2 : 1100
 What is the content of R1 and R2 after execution of this micro-operation?
 R1 ← R1 ⊕ R2
 ⊕ is a symbol of Ex-OR.
qs.sol:
Step 1: Perform Ex-OR operation between R1 (1010) and R2 (1100).

Step 2: Bit-by-bit Ex-OR: 1⊕1=0, 0⊕1=1, 1⊕0=1, 0⊕0=0.

Step 3: Result is 0110, which updates R1.

Step 4: R2 remains unchanged as 1100.

qs.stem: Which of the following floating point numbers is represented by the 0 1000 0011 1001 0100 0000 0000 0000 000 in IEEE 754 standard?
qs.sol: First, parse the 32-bit binary string into IEEE 754 single precision components. The sign bit is 0, indicating a positive number. The exponent bits are 1000 0011, which equals 131 in decimal. Subtracting the bias of 127 gives an actual exponent of 4. The mantissa bits represent a fraction that combines with the implicit leading one to form 1.578125. Finally, multiply this significand by 2 to the power of 4 to get the final value of 25.25.

qs.stem: If the value of multiplicand is 10111 and multiplier is 10011, what will be the result produced by Booth’s multiplication algorithm in decimal?
qs.sol:
Booth's method treats these five-bit operands as signed two's-complement values: 10111 is −9 and 10011 is −13.

Their product is 117.

qs.stem:
The 8-bit register A and B initially have the following values:
 A = 01110110
 B = 10000101
 What is the 8-bit value in each register after execution of the following micro-operation?
 A ← A + B
 B ← B + 1
qs.sol:
Step 1: Perform binary addition of A and B: 01110110 + 10000101.

Step 2: Add bit by bit from right to left, including carry.

Step 3: The sum is 11111011 with a carry-out of 1, which is discarded in 8-bit arithmetic.

Step 4: Increment B by 1: 10000101 + 1 = 10000110.

Final values: A = 11111011, B = 10000110.

topics.title: 7. Multimedia, Image/Audio Formats & MS Office
topics.theory:
- **Image formats:** **JPEG = Joint Photographic Experts Group** (lossy, photos); **GIF = Graphics Interchange Format** (**256 colours, 8-bit palette**, supports animation & 1-bit transparency); PNG (lossless, alpha); BMP/**.DIB = Device Independent Bitmap**; WMF/EMF = Windows (Enhanced) Metafile (vector); **WAV is audio, not an image format**. **Colour depth:** 8 bpp = 256 colours = **palette images**; **16 bpp = high colour**; 24 bpp = true colour.
- **Audio/video:** **MPEG audio = .mp3 (MPEG-1 Layer 3)**; MPEG-4 = .mp4; MPEG macroblock = **16×16 pixels**; **MIDI = Musical Instrument Digital Interface**; **digitisation uses sampling and quantisation**; **data compression** reduces file size. **Haptic technology** = **tactile** (touch) feedback.
- **Authoring tools:** **PowerPoint = card/slide-based** (as per exam key); **Flash/Director = time-based**; Authorware/IconAuthor = **icon-based** (flowline); **HyperCard = card-based, created for Mac**; **Lingo = scripting language of Macromedia/Adobe Director**. **Flash keyframes:** **F6 = insert keyframe, F5 = insert frame, F7 = blank keyframe; Shift+F6 = delete keyframe/clear**; a keyframe holds a change.
- **MS Word shortcuts:** **Ctrl+Z undo**, Ctrl+Y redo, **Ctrl+R right-align**, **Ctrl+J justify**, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+L left, **Ctrl+T hanging indent**, **Ctrl+H find & replace**, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+Enter page break, **Ctrl+] increase font by 1 pt**, Ctrl+[ decrease. **Excel:** workbook = file (contains sheets); **Ctrl+G / F5 = Go To**. **PowerPoint:** background for all slides is set in the **Slide Master**; enhances presentations with pictures, charts, sound, video, animation.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not the file formats of graphics?

A graphics file format is a file format used to store image data - pixel colour values (raster) or path/shape data (vector) - so that visual content can be displayed or edited.

Checking each option against this definition: GIF, JPG, and PNG are all raster image file formats that store picture data, so all three qualify as graphics formats. This question asks specifically for the extension of an MPEG AUDIO file (not a full MPEG video stream). MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III audio files are universally saved and recognized with the .mp3 extension, so .mp3 is the correct choice here. …
